title: 1 Samuel Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 11.

questions.question: Who came up and encamped against Jabeshgilead?
questions.correctAnswer: Nahash the Ammonite
questions.explanation: Nahash the Ammonite came up and encamped against Jabeshgilead as stated in 1 Samuel 11:1.

questions.question: What did all the men of Jabesh say to Nahash?
options: Make a covenant with us, and we will serve thee
questions.correctAnswer: Make a covenant with us, and we will serve thee
questions.explanation: The men of Jabesh requested Nahash to make a covenant with them and promised to serve him as described in 1 Samuel 11:1.

questions.question: What condition did Nahash set for making a covenant with the men of Jabesh?
options: He would thrust out all their right eyes
questions.correctAnswer: He would thrust out all their right eyes
questions.explanation: Nahash said he would make a covenant only on the condition that he might thrust out all their right eyes, as found in 1 Samuel 11:2.

questions.question: What did the elders of Jabesh request from Nahash after hearing his condition?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven days' respite
questions.explanation: The elders of Jabesh asked for seven days' respite to send messengers throughout Israel, shown in 1 Samuel 11:3.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the seven days' respite requested by the elders of Jabesh?
options: To send messengers to all the coasts of Israel
To negotiate a better deal with Nahash
questions.correctAnswer: To send messengers to all the coasts of Israel
questions.explanation: The elders wanted seven days to send messengers to all the coasts of Israel to seek help as in 1 Samuel 11:3.

questions.question: Where did the messengers go to deliver the tidings about Jabesh?
questions.correctAnswer: Gibeah of Saul
questions.explanation: The messengers came to Gibeah of Saul to tell the people the news, according to 1 Samuel 11:4.

questions.question: How did the people respond when they heard the tidings of Jabesh from the messengers?
options: They lifted up their voices, and wept
questions.correctAnswer: They lifted up their voices, and wept
questions.explanation: The people lifted up their voices and wept upon hearing the news, as stated in 1 Samuel 11:4.

questions.question: Who came out of the field after the herd and asked why the people were weeping?
questions.correctAnswer: Saul
questions.explanation: Saul came after the herd and asked about the cause of the weeping, as recorded in 1 Samuel 11:5.

questions.question: What was Saul’s reaction when he heard the tidings of Jabesh?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The Spirit of God came upon Saul and his anger was kindled greatly when he heard the tidings, according to 1 Samuel 11:6.

questions.question: True or False: Saul sent messengers throughout Israel threatening to do the same to their oxen if they did not come out to fight.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Saul took a yoke of oxen, hewed them in pieces, and sent messengers with a threat that the same would be done to their oxen if they did not follow him, as seen in 1 Samuel 11:7.

questions.question: How many men of Israel were numbered in Bezek by Saul?
questions.correctAnswer: Three hundred thousand
questions.explanation: In Bezek, Saul numbered three hundred thousand men of Israel and thirty thousand men of Judah, as stated in 1 Samuel 11:8.

questions.question: What message were the messengers instructed to give to the men of Jabeshgilead?
options: That help would come by the time the sun was hot the next day
That they should flee the city
questions.correctAnswer: That help would come by the time the sun was hot the next day
questions.explanation: The messengers were told to say that by the next day, by the time the sun was hot, help would arrive, as in 1 Samuel 11:9.

questions.question: True or False: The men of Jabesh were glad when they heard the message of coming help.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The men of Jabesh were glad upon hearing the message that help was coming, as stated in 1 Samuel 11:9.

questions.question: In what order did the following happen in 1 Samuel 11: (1) Saul numbered the men at Bezek, (2) the elders of Jabesh requested seven days, (3) the messengers reported to Gibeah of Saul, (4) Saul threatened to cut up oxen?
questions.explanation: The elders of Jabesh requested seven days' respite (verse 3), then messengers reported to Gibeah (verse 4), Saul threatened with oxen (verse 7), and later he numbered the men at Bezek (verse 8).

questions.question: True or False: The men of Jabesh agreed to come out to Nahash without conditions after the seven days.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The men of Jabesh said they would come out to Nahash and let him do whatever seemed good to him, which implies conditions, as seen in 1 Samuel 11:10.

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What happened to Saul when he heard the tidings about Jabeshgilead and Nahash the Ammonite?
options: The Spirit of God came upon him and his anger was kindled
He sent peace offerings to Nahash
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit of God came upon him and his anger was kindled
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 11:6 states that the Spirit of God came upon Saul when he heard the tidings, and his anger was kindled greatly. This shows his divine empowerment and righteous anger in response to the threat.

questions.question: How did Saul demonstrate leadership to rally Israel against the Ammonites?
options: He cut oxen into pieces and sent them to all Israel to call for support
He wrote letters to neighboring nations
He sent messengers to Jabeshgilead to negotiate peace
questions.correctAnswer: He cut oxen into pieces and sent them to all Israel to call for support
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 11:7 describes how Saul took a yoke of oxen, hewed them in pieces, and sent them throughout Israel as a call to arms, emphasizing the seriousness of the situation and uniting the people.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 11:7-8, what was the reaction of the people to Saul's message and what was the size of the assembled army?
options: The fear of the LORD fell on the people, and they came out with one consent; 300,000 Israelites and 30,000 men of Judah
The people ignored Saul's call; 10,000 men assembled
There was confusion and division; 50,000 men assembled
The people demanded peace talks; 100,000 men assembled
questions.correctAnswer: The fear of the LORD fell on the people, and they came out with one consent; 300,000 Israelites and 30,000 men of Judah
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 show that Saul's call inspired unity and reverence for God, leading to a large army of 300,000 Israelites and 30,000 men of Judah assembling at Bezek.

questions.question: What message was sent to the men of Jabeshgilead regarding the coming help?
options: Tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, you shall have help
We will negotiate with Nahash tonight
You must surrender to the Ammonites
questions.correctAnswer: Tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, you shall have help
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 11:9 records the message sent to Jabeshgilead, promising timely assistance, which brought gladness to the men there, showing God's providential care through Saul's leadership.

questions.question: How did the men of Jabeshgilead respond to the promise of help from Israel?
options: They said they would come out to Israel and submit to whatever seemed good
They refused to trust the promise and prepared for battle
They sent more messengers to delay the attack
questions.correctAnswer: They said they would come out to Israel and submit to whatever seemed good
questions.explanation: Verse 10 shows the men of Jabesh expressing trust and humility, willing to accept whatever Israel decided, demonstrating faith and reliance on God's deliverance through His people.

questions.question: In what way does Saul's action of cutting oxen and sending the pieces teach about Christian leadership and obedience?
options: It teaches that bold, decisive actions can unify believers in times of crisis
It shows leaders should avoid confrontation
It encourages secrecy over open communication
It suggests waiting for divine signs before acting
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that bold, decisive actions can unify believers in times of crisis
questions.explanation: Based on verses 7-8, Saul's bold symbolic act mobilized the entire nation, showing that faithful leadership involves courageous, clear calls to action inspiring unity and obedience.

questions.question: True or False: The Spirit of God came upon Saul before he heard the news about Jabeshgilead.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 11:6 specifies that the Spirit of God came upon Saul when he heard the tidings, indicating the Spirit's arrival was in direct response to the news.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 11:7 promise will happen if a man does not come out after Saul and Samuel as instructed?
options: His oxen will be hewed in pieces as a punishment
He will be given a warning
questions.correctAnswer: His oxen will be hewed in pieces as a punishment
questions.explanation: Verse 7 clearly states the consequence is that the same fate of being hewed in pieces will befall the man's oxen, symbolizing the seriousness of obedience and unity in God's cause.

questions.question: How does the response of the men of Jabeshgilead (verse 10) teach about humility and trust in God during trials?
options: They submit to whatever is decided, showing trust and humility in God's deliverance
They demand specific terms for their safety
They refuse to cooperate with Israel
They rely solely on their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: They submit to whatever is decided, showing trust and humility in God's deliverance
questions.explanation: Verse 10 shows Jabeshgilead's humble and trusting attitude, accepting Israel's help and judgment, teaching believers to trust God's provision and be humble in adversity.

questions.question: What virtue does Saul's swift mobilization of the army illustrate for Christians facing urgent challenges?
options: Obedience and prompt action guided by the Spirit of God
Waiting passively for events to unfold
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience and prompt action guided by the Spirit of God
questions.explanation: Verses 6-8 highlight Saul's Spirit-empowered immediate response, teaching believers to obey and act swiftly under God's guidance when facing urgent matters.

questions.question: True or False: The assembled army at Bezek consisted of only men from Judah.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 11:8 specifies the army included 300,000 men from Israel and 30,000 from Judah, showing unity across tribes rather than only Judah.

questions.question: How does the passage about the messengers bringing glad tidings to Jabeshgilead (verse 9) teach about the impact of hopeful news?
options: Hopeful news can bring joy and strengthen faith in difficult times
Good news should be kept secret
questions.correctAnswer: Hopeful news can bring joy and strengthen faith in difficult times
questions.explanation: Verse 9 shows that the men of Jabesh were glad upon hearing they would receive help, illustrating how hope and encouragement are vital for perseverance.

questions.question: What practical lesson about trust in God's deliverance can be drawn from the interaction between Saul's call and the people’s response?
options: Trusting God's appointed leaders mobilizes collective action and victory
Isolation is the best response to danger
Leaders should rely on their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting God's appointed leaders mobilizes collective action and victory
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 11:7-8 reveals that the people responded with fear of the LORD and unity under Saul and Samuel, showing that faith in God and His leaders leads to effective action.

questions.question: How might 1 Samuel 11 encourage a believer who feels overwhelmed by a challenge today?
options: To trust God's Spirit to empower them and to rally support through bold action
To isolate themselves and avoid involvement
To ignore the problem and hope it goes away
To act independently without seeking counsel
questions.correctAnswer: To trust God's Spirit to empower them and to rally support through bold action
questions.explanation: The chapter shows how Saul was empowered by God's Spirit (verse 6) and took decisive action (verse 7), teaching believers to rely on God and seek communal support in challenges.

questions.question: True or False: The men of Jabeshgilead requested a seven-day respite to seek help from Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Although this event is described in verse 3, it is part of the broader context of the chapter and important to understand the timing of Israel's response.

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 11.

questions.question: How many companies did Saul divide the people into when he attacked the Ammonites?
questions.correctAnswer: Three
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 11:11 states that Saul put the people in three companies before the attack.

questions.question: What was the result of Saul's attack on the Ammonites according to the chapter?
options: They were scattered so that not two were left together
questions.correctAnswer: They were scattered so that not two were left together
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 11:11 explains that the remaining Ammonites were scattered, so that two of them were not left together.

questions.question: After Saul's victory, what did the people want to do to those who opposed Saul's reign?
options: Bring them to Samuel to be put to death
questions.correctAnswer: Bring them to Samuel to be put to death
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 11:12 states the people said to Samuel, 'Who is he that said, Shall Saul reign over us? bring the men, that we may put them to death.'

questions.question: What was Saul's response to the people's desire to kill those opposing his reign?
options: He agreed to put them to death immediately
He refused and said no man would be put to death that day
He asked Samuel to judge them
questions.correctAnswer: He refused and said no man would be put to death that day
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 11:13 records Saul saying that no man would be put to death that day because the LORD had wrought salvation in Israel.

questions.question: Where did Samuel invite the people to go to renew the kingdom after Saul's victory?
questions.correctAnswer: Gilgal
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 11:14 records Samuel saying, 'Come, and let us go to Gilgal, and renew the kingdom there.'

questions.question: What significant event took place at Gilgal involving Saul and all the men of Israel?
options: They renewed the kingdom and made Saul king before the LORD
They wrote the law of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: They renewed the kingdom and made Saul king before the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 11:15 states that Saul was made king before the LORD in Gilgal and the people rejoiced greatly.

questions.question: What type of sacrifices were offered at Gilgal when Saul was made king?
questions.correctAnswer: Peace offerings
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 11:15 mentions the sacrifices of peace offerings before the LORD at Gilgal.

questions.question: The Spirit of God coming upon Saul when he heard the tidings most closely foreshadows which New Testament event?
questions.correctAnswer: Pentecost in Acts 2
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 11:6 describes the Spirit of God coming upon Saul, which foreshadows the coming of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost in Acts 2, empowering God's chosen leaders.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'yoke' in 1 Samuel 11:7 symbolizes what in the context of Saul's message?
questions.correctAnswer: Burden and judgment
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 11:7, the 'yoke of oxen' refers to a burden; Saul cut them and threatened the same fate upon those who would not follow him, symbolizing judgment.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in the narrative that frames Saul’s rise with the deliverance of Jabeshgilead?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The chapter begins and ends focusing on the deliverance of Jabeshgilead and Saul's kingship, creating an inclusio framing Saul’s rise with the victory (1 Samuel 11:1 and 11:15).

questions.question: True or False: Saul ordered his men to attack the Ammonites at midday when the sun was hottest.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 11:11 states Saul attacked during the morning watch and continued until the heat of the day, not starting at midday.

questions.question: True or False: The people of Israel unanimously supported Saul's leadership after his victory over the Ammonites.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The people came out with one consent after Saul’s call (1 Samuel 11:7) and rejoiced greatly after his kingship was confirmed (1 Samuel 11:15).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage parallels the theme of God delivering His people through a chosen leader as seen in 1 Samuel 11?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 14:13-14
questions.explanation: Exodus 14:13-14 shows God delivering Israel through Moses, paralleling Saul’s deliverance of Jabeshgilead and Israel in 1 Samuel 11.

questions.question: How does the chapter 11 of 1 Samuel reflect the ancient Near Eastern practice of kingship?
options: Kings often demonstrated power through military might and covenant renewal
Kingship was hereditary without public consent
questions.correctAnswer: Kings often demonstrated power through military might and covenant renewal
questions.explanation: Saul’s military leadership and the renewal of the kingdom at Gilgal (1 Samuel 11:14-15) reflect the Near Eastern model where kings legitimize their rule through war and religious ceremonies.

questions.question: Which New Testament figure echoes the theme of salvation wrought by God as declared by Saul in 1 Samuel 11:13?
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: Saul’s declaration that the LORD wrought salvation (1 Samuel 11:13) foreshadows Jesus Christ as the ultimate Savior in the New Testament (Luke 2:30-32).

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Nahash's demand to thrust out the right eyes of the men of Jabeshgilead symbolize in the context of divine justice and human sinfulness?
options: A call for physical mutilation as a form of retribution
A symbol of Israel’s vulnerability and impending judgment
An act demonstrating God's mercy to Israel
A political strategy to gain control over Israel
questions.correctAnswer: A symbol of Israel’s vulnerability and impending judgment
questions.explanation: Nahash's demand to thrust out the right eyes was to lay a reproach upon all Israel, symbolizing their vulnerability and judgment (1 Samuel 11:2). This reflects the doctrine of human sinfulness exposing Israel to divine discipline.

questions.question: How does Saul’s reaction upon hearing the plight of Jabeshgilead illustrate the attribute of God’s Spirit operating in human agents?
options: It shows human anger without divine influence
It demonstrates the Spirit of God empowering leadership for deliverance
It reflects a natural military strategy without spiritual significance
It indicates fear and hesitation in decision-making
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates the Spirit of God empowering leadership for deliverance
questions.explanation: Verse 6 states the Spirit of God came upon Saul, kindling his anger and prompting decisive action, illustrating divine empowerment in human leadership (1 Samuel 11:6). This shows the attribute of God’s active presence in salvation history.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is taught by Saul’s method of rallying Israel with the threat against oxen?
options: The necessity of fear as a motivation for obedience
God’s sovereign use of human agency and social cohesion for salvation
The futility of human effort without divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereign use of human agency and social cohesion for salvation
questions.explanation: Saul cutting oxen and sending the pieces as a summons shows God using human means and collective responsibility to unify Israel for deliverance (1 Samuel 11:7). It teaches God's providential orchestration of salvation through human cooperation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated by the fear of the LORD falling upon the people after Saul’s summons?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: The fear of the LORD causing the people to unite shows His sovereign control over human hearts and events (1 Samuel 11:7). God's sovereignty ensures His plans for Israel’s salvation prevail.

questions.question: How does the numerical strength of Israel and Judah in verse 8 contribute to the theological understanding of God’s providence in salvation history?
options: It reveals human strength as the cause of victory
It emphasizes divine providence in assembling a prepared people
It shows numerical superiority guarantees success
It indicates political alliances more than divine action
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes divine providence in assembling a prepared people
questions.explanation: The large number of men assembled reflects God’s providential preparation of Israel to fulfill His purpose of deliverance (1 Samuel 11:8). This supports the doctrine of God’s providence in history.

questions.question: What theological insight can be derived from the men of Jabeshgilead expressing gladness upon hearing of the promised help?
options: It demonstrates human despair without hope
It illustrates faith and trust in God’s deliverance through His anointed
It reflects confidence in military strength alone
It shows indifference to divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates faith and trust in God’s deliverance through His anointed
questions.explanation: Their gladness at the promise of help (1 Samuel 11:9) reveals trust in God’s intervention by means of Saul, God’s anointed king, illustrating the doctrine of faith in divine salvation.

questions.question: Which doctrine is best illustrated by the complete defeat and scattering of the Ammonites by Saul’s forces?
options: God’s sovereign judgment on Israel’s enemies
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereign judgment on Israel’s enemies
questions.explanation: The total defeat of the Ammonites (1 Samuel 11:11) demonstrates God's sovereign judgment and protection of His covenant people, affirming His justice and faithfulness.

questions.question: How does Saul’s refusal to put to death those who opposed his reign on the day of battle reflect a theological understanding of salvation and grace?
options: It shows Saul’s weakness and indecision
It exemplifies divine mercy and the preservation of life after salvation
It indicates political expediency over justice
It reflects disregard for covenant law
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies divine mercy and the preservation of life after salvation
questions.explanation: Saul’s refusal to execute opponents (1 Samuel 11:13) reflects the doctrine of grace and mercy extended to Israel, as salvation had been wrought that day by the LORD, showing God’s merciful preservation.

questions.question: What redemptive narrative significance does the renewal of the kingdom at Gilgal hold in 1 Samuel 11:14-15?
options: It marks only a political event with no spiritual meaning
It symbolizes the establishment of God's covenantal kingship in Israel
It is a mere military celebration without theological import
It indicates rejection of prior leadership
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the establishment of God's covenantal kingship in Israel
questions.explanation: The renewal of the kingdom at Gilgal (1 Samuel 11:14-15) signifies God’s covenantal kingship being established through Saul, foreshadowing the Messianic kingdom and God's sovereign rule.

questions.question: How do the combined verses 5-6 and 11 demonstrate the theological connection between divine inspiration and victorious salvation?
options: They show human emotions as primary in warfare
They reveal the Spirit of God empowering Saul leading to Israel’s salvation
They emphasize coincidence rather than divine action
They suggest Saul’s victory was by chance
questions.correctAnswer: They reveal the Spirit of God empowering Saul leading to Israel’s salvation
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 highlight the Spirit of God coming upon Saul when hearing the news, and verse 11 shows the resulting victorious battle, together teaching that divine inspiration empowers deliverance (1 Samuel 11:5-6, 11).

questions.question: What doctrinal synthesis emerges from combining verses 1 and 12 regarding Israel’s response to external threat and internal dissent?
options: Israel’s rejection of kingship weakens their defense
External threat unites Israel while internal dissent causes division
God uses external threats to unify Israel despite internal rebellion
Israel’s internal dissent is more dangerous than external enemies
questions.correctAnswer: God uses external threats to unify Israel despite internal rebellion
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows the external Ammonite threat, and verse 12 reveals internal dissent about Saul’s kingship, together teaching that God’s providence uses external crisis to unify Israel even amid internal opposition (1 Samuel 11:1, 12).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Israel’s military success under Saul was purely due to human strategy and luck. What does 1 Samuel 11:7-11 actually teach about the source of Israel’s victory?
options: Victory was accidental and unrelated to God
The Spirit of God empowered Saul and the fear of the LORD united the people, resulting in victory
The victory was due to superior numbers alone
Ammonite weakness was the sole factor in Israel’s win
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit of God empowered Saul and the fear of the LORD united the people, resulting in victory
questions.explanation: Verses 7-11 reveal that God’s Spirit empowered Saul and the fear of the LORD caused Israel’s unity and courage, resulting in decisive victory, refuting sceptical claims of mere chance (1 Samuel 11:7-11; cf. Exodus 15:6).

questions.question: What theological truth about God's covenant faithfulness is illustrated when the men of Jabeshgilead seek a covenant with Nahash, yet God delivers them through Saul instead?
options: God always allows humans to choose their own deliverance
God’s covenant faithfulness transcends human compromise and provides true salvation
Human alliances are better than trusting God
God’s covenant is conditional on military strength
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant faithfulness transcends human compromise and provides true salvation
questions.explanation: The men of Jabesh sought a covenant with Nahash (1 Samuel 11:1), but God’s faithfulness is shown by delivering them through Saul, teaching that God alone provides true salvation beyond human compromises.

questions.question: How does the chapter’s narrative arc from threat to victorious kingly enthronement (verses 1–15) deepen our understanding of God’s redemptive plan in history?
options: It shows God’s plan unfolds through human kingship anointed by Him
It proves human kingship is flawed and rejected by God
It suggests that God’s plan is purely political
It indicates God acts only sporadically in history
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God’s plan unfolds through human kingship anointed by Him
questions.explanation: The progression from threat (v.1) through Spirit-empowered victory (v.6-11) to Saul’s enthronement (v.14-15) reveals God’s redemptive plan working through His anointed king, pointing forward to Christ as ultimate King (1 Samuel 11:1-15).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most evident in the people’s unanimous response to Saul’s call despite their previous dissent?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s unifying sovereignty
questions.explanation: The people’s unified response (1 Samuel 11:7) despite earlier dissent (v.12) displays God’s unifying sovereignty over Israel, orchestrating their cooperation for salvation.
